# Pinned offline voice decoders

Only the link-reachable decoder source units and their header closure are vendored. No encoder implementation, SDK test tools, prebuilt binaries, real media or upstream git history is included. `manifest.json` pins every unmodified upstream source/header by SHA-256 and explicitly lists 54 SILK + 76 AMR compilation units. `tools/build_codecs.py` verifies these hashes before compiling; it downloads and installs nothing. macOS builds one runner-native test architecture, iOS builds arm64 only.

- SILK SDK from kn007/silk-v3-decoder commit `507be6bca8ce1fb977a061481f1d79e8c610e309`, `silk/`. Preserve Skype's BSD-style conditions in each file and `silk/LICENSE`. The repository's outer MIT license is not a substitute for the SDK license.
- OpenCORE AMR source identifies itself as 0.1.3 (`opencore-amr-master` archived source used for the established fixtures). Archive SHA-256: `ac1957694e8501e1ca1aee0929e736865c175bad55fa8429931e8e35c3155ad1`. Exact selected files are pinned in the manifest rather than following master. Apache-2.0 `amr/LICENSE` and upstream `amr/NOTICE` are preserved without truncation.
- Binary distributions MUST carry both licenses and NOTICE; build.sh includes them in the artifact. These licenses do not constitute a patent clearance or any patent guarantee. Skype expressly grants no patent rights. No legal assurance of jurisdiction-specific patent freedom is made.

## Production contract

`WUVoiceDecode` routes standard `#!SILK_V3`, Tencent `0x02 + #!SILK_V3`, and AMR-NB `#!AMR\n` through `OfflineVoice.c`. SILK explicitly requests 16000 Hz; AMR-NB always produces 8000 Hz. Both SDKs emit mono signed int16 native-endian samples (little-endian on iOS arm64 and supported macOS runners), converted numerically to mono float for existing real peak buckets and duration = frames / rate. No host PCM contract is inferred. Peak/duration output is consumed by existing UI and host millisecond seek; original messages and playback files are never modified.

SILK packet lengths are little-endian signed-16 values: 1..5120 accepted, optional -1 terminal marker only at EOF. AMR storage TOC must have clear F/reserved bits, good quality and FT 0..8 with exact payload length. FT 9..15 (including NO_DATA), AMR-WB and concealment requests are intentionally unsupported, rather than inventing PCM. Codec errors, truncation, zero/invalid lengths, appended malformed frames or cancellation discard all PCM, not partial success. Bit flips that remain valid codec syntax cannot universally be detected (these formats have no general integrity checksum).

Limits: encoded 8 MiB; 9000 packets; 5 internal SILK frames/packet; 180 seconds; maximum float buffer 11,520,000 bytes plus decoder state <=1 MiB and encoded input. Reallocation may transiently hold old plus new buffer (<=~20 MiB combined PCM buffers). Serial background queue limits concurrent decoder work. Cancellation uses a request-specific thread-safe NSProgress, checked per packet and before delivery; request/account/generation/view/foreground checks reject stale UI results. A fully truncated file exactly at a valid frame boundary has no declared total duration to compare and is inherently indistinguishable from a shorter complete file.

The SDKs use legacy fixed-point arithmetic: build with the tested `-O2` semantics. Adding `-fwrapv` changed AMR output on GCC in the new production regression; it is deliberately not added. Native CI checks actual decoded sample peaks and duration, not just compilation. No encoder is built, no additional codec framework or network service is added.
